title: St. Louis City to sign Carlo Holse as designated player after $6M transfer: Sources
content:
St. Louis City has reached an agreement to sign Danish attacker Carlo Holse from Samsunspor, sources briefed on the deal tell The Athletic.

The clubs are in agreement on a fee worth around $6 million, sources add. Holse will be a designated player when the deal is completed.

Holse, 27, had eight goals and four assists in the Turkish Süper Lig last season. He has been with Samsunspor since 2023 and has been a key contributor since arriving, with at least eight goal contributions each season.

The attacker was a key figure for the club’s run to the UEFA Conference League round of 16, with two goals and five assists in 10 appearances in the competition.

Before moving to Turkey, Holse starred for Norwegian side Rosenborg. His career began with FC Copenhagen in Denmark.

Holse represents a significant addition for St. Louis, which now has another marquee attacker alongside Marcel Hartel. The team is being rebuilt under new leadership and head coach Yoann Damet.

The roster needed to be overturned to fit Damet’s possession-based ethos, and plenty of work has been done to reshape the group. The club was targeting a DP this summer, and Holse, who has one cap for Denmark’s national team (as a substitute for San Diego FC DP Anders Dreyer in June 2025 vs. Lithuania), is the guy.

Holse can play alongside Hartel in the team’s dual No. 10 slots in Damet’s preferred 3-4-2-1. He can be a primary creator — he had 16 assists in one league season for Rosenborg — or take on some of the goal-scoring burden as well. St. Louis, could use the attacking boost, as only five clubs have scored fewer than its 19 goals so far this season.

St. Louis sits 10th place in the West, just one point behind the LA Galaxy for the final playoff spot with 19 games remaining.
